idiom_name: enum Message + update(&mut Model, Message) + view(&Model), wired by hand over a channel
implementation_notes: Rust's type system fits the pure part naturally - intents are exhaustive enums, the reducer is a match that transitions the model, and view(&Model) borrows the state read-only so only update can change it - but no standard library supplies the runtime, so the state holder, the intent queue and the subscription are hand-written (a channel plus a loop, or a framework). When a full framework is acceptable, iced implements exactly this loop: State, Messages, view logic and update logic with iced::run(update, view), which makes it the closest thing to a Rust MVI substrate; egui-style immediate-mode tools instead keep state in one struct and redraw, which is the simpler alternative for a small tool. Hand-writing is the default because no Rust GUI framework is dominant and the pattern is usually chosen for the purity the enum/match form gives.
pitfalls: &mut Model lets update perform partial transitions; switch to fn update(model: Model, msg: Message) -> Model when snapshots must be immutable for diffing or history.
An unbounded mpsc/crossbeam channel of messages grows without limit when the view floods intents; bound the queue or coalesce intents before the loop.
Sending state to subscribers through channels requires Clone, and deep clones of a large state on every transition are the usual performance trap; share Arc<State> instead.
Capturing a UI toolkit handle (winit/egui context) inside the model makes the state non-Send and non-serializable; keep it in effects, not in the state.
